en.title: Maximum Grayness of a Pixel Matrix
en.description:
The grayness of cell (i,j) equals the total number of 1s minus the total number of 0s in its row and its column; the intersection cell is counted once in the row and once in the column. Find the maximum grayness.

The standard input/output, examples and judging were written independently by CSWork; conventions marked as this site's do not pass themselves off as the source's original limits.
en.input: The first line contains n m (both 1..1000), followed by n lines of 01 strings of length m.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: the first row and the first column each have two 1s and one 0, so the grayness is (2+2)−(1+1)=2. Example 2: the only 0 is counted once in its row and once in its column, so the grayness is −2. Example 3: every row and column has two 1s, so the maximum grayness is 4.
hints: Count the 1s in each row and in each column; the maximum grayness is 2×(max 1s in a row+max 1s in a column)−n−m.
